COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
09.01.2023 AO No.152 of 2022
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J. s
Heard Mr. Deepak Rawat, learned 
counsel for the appellant – Insurance 
Company and Mr. Bharat Singh, learned 
counsel for the respondent no.1 – claimant 
on the Money Withdrawal Application (IA 
No.02 of 2022).
Learned counsel for the appellant –
Insurance Company submitted that the 
Insurance Company has deposited 50% 
amount of the awarded amount. 
Learned Motor Accident Claims 
Tribunal/IVth Additional District Judge, 
Haridwar has passed the Award dated 
10.11.2021 in Claim Petition No.121 of 
2016, “Smt. Neelu vs. Siyanand and 
Others”, by which, the learned Tribunal has 
awarded a total sum of Rs.1,44,35,930/-
along with an interest at the rate of 6% per 
annum from the date of petition till its 
actual payment.
Having regard to the submissions of 
the learned counsel for the parties, the 
Tribunal concerned is directed to release 
Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakhs) out of the 
said deposited amount in favour of the 
respondent no.1 – claimant, namely, Smt. 
Neelu, in accordance with law.
The Money Withdrawal Application (IA 
No.02 of 2022) is disposed of accordingly.
List this case on 02.05.2023.
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) 
 09.01.2023
Pant/

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
A.O. No. 152 of 2022
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Deepak Rawat, counsel for the appellant/Insurance 
Company.
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, counsel for the 
respondents/claimants.
2. Counsel for the appellant would submit that the Tribunal 
grossly erred in assessing the disability of the claimant at 100% 
for the purposes of calculating the compensation whereas in the 
disability certificate issued by the Medical Board, the disability 
of the injured had been assessed as 70%, therefore, the 
impugned award is not sustainable in the eyes of law. 
3. Per contra, counsel for the respondents/claimants would 
submit that due to the injury received in the accident, the 
respondent no.1/claimant is unable to do any work and needed 
attendant for doing her routine work; that, the respondent 
no./claimant is unable to speak and understands the basic things 
as she in third stage of coma due to injury received in the 
accident on her head, she requires an attendant who help her to 
do routine work and such attendant will not come at the cost of 
less than `25,000/- per month. 
4. Counsel for the parties seeks and is granted time to place 
law in support of their submissions.
5. Put up on 07.12.2023.
6. Interim order dated 09.05.2022 to continue till the next 
date of listing.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) 12.10.2023 Mamta
